source.title: Extending and Analyzing Self-Supervised Learning Across Domains

page_placements.theme: Frozen-representation probes separate semantic and arbitrary-label fitting

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains linear classifiers on learned features with randomly shuffled training labels and compares training accuracy against correct-label training accuracy. This bears conceptually on random-label fit but does not test the original end-to-end network memorization claim.
record.gate_note: The random-label experiment retrains linear classifiers on learned features and reports correlations with normal-label training accuracy plus a qualitative conclusion. It does not report zero training error, test error at chance, training-time cost, shuffled or Gaussian inputs, or performance across corruption fractions. Other cited random-label work is not extracted.
record.test_reason: The random-label experiment measures linear separability of frozen self-supervised representations. Only linear classifiers are retrained; the deep networks are not trained to fit random labels. Correlations between normal-label and random-label training accuracy do not establish any claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases Section 5.3: the stronger correlation for Jigsaw is interpreted as greater reliance on generic image descriptors rather than downstream semantics. The authors explicitly restrict this experiment to training accuracy and say it does not explain generalization to unseen data.
record.recipe_differences: Randomly shuffled labels are used to retrain linear classifiers on self-supervised features; this is not the original end-to-end random-label memorization experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: Across datasets, normal-label and shuffled-label training accuracies correlate at r = 0.59 for Jigsaw, 0.46 for Instance Discrimination, and 0.45 for Rotation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Frozen self-supervised representations differ in how closely their linear classifiers' ability to fit arbitrary labelings tracks their ability to fit semantic labels.

record.problems: The random-label results are reported as correlations across tasks, without the individual random-label training accuracies or random-label test error. The authors state that this experiment does not reveal generalization to data outside the training set.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 8 plots per-task differences between normal and random-label training accuracy, but the supplied text gives no recoverable numerical values; figure-only points were not transcribed. No cited prior-work results were extracted.

untested.parts: End-to-end deep-network fitting of completely random labels to zero or near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Relative fitting time and convergence as label corruption increases.
Perfect fitting of shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error across corruption fractions.
Whether explicit regularization prevents random-label memorization and whether removing it alone harms true-label generalization. The stated omission of weight decay supplies no controlled test.
The temporal ordering of learning shared real-data patterns and memorizing noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: Table 2's caption calls the Instance Discrimination correlation significant despite reporting p = 0.07; no significance threshold is supplied. Figure 8's untranscribed results are already declared in rows_left_out and concern the same linear-classifier diagnostic.

versions.untested_parts: Tests random-label training accuracy only for retrained linear classifiers on learned features; does not report exact random-label accuracies or show zero/near-zero error, chance test error, or unchanged end-to-end network and optimizer settings.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Section 5.3 studies shuffled-label fitting by linear classifiers on learned features, a related construct rather than the claimed end-to-end deep-network behavior.

tranche.reason: The experiment measures linear separability of self-supervised representations through correlations across datasets. It neither tests a claim version nor uses deep-network random-label memorization as a tool.

source_check.notes: The authors restrict the random-label analysis to training accuracy and explicitly say it does not explain generalization. Table 2's caption calls the ID correlation significant, although its reported p-value is 0.07.
